name: security/csrf
summary: Protect cookie-authenticated state-changing web requests from cross-site request forgery.
intent: Browser requests that rely on automatically attached credentials cannot perform protected state changes from an untrusted origin, while legitimate application requests and non-cookie API authentication keep working.

rules.text: State-changing browser routes that rely on cookie credentials require a server-verifiable CSRF defense.
Legitimate same-application requests can obtain or present the value or origin proof required by the chosen CSRF defense.
A missing, invalid, or mismatched CSRF proof is rejected before the protected state change runs.

invariants.text: Read-only safe-method requests are not made state-changing merely to work around CSRF enforcement.
Non-cookie API authentication paths are not forced into a browser CSRF mechanism when credentials are not automatically attached cross-site.
Existing session creation, rotation, and logout semantics remain intact.

security.text: Any CSRF secret or token entropy is generated server-side or cryptographically and is not predictable from public account data.
Origin or referer validation, when used, compares against trusted configured origins rather than request-controlled host values.
CORS configuration is not treated as the sole CSRF defense for cookie-authenticated state changes.
Cookie SameSite settings are treated as defense in depth and remain compatible with the application's legitimate cross-site flows.

acceptance.text: A legitimate protected browser request with the required proof succeeds and performs the state change.
The same protected request without CSRF proof is rejected before the state change executes.
A proof bound to the wrong session, secret, or origin is rejected.
A non-cookie API authentication path keeps its intended behavior without receiving unnecessary CSRF coupling.
